## Critique
- claim-1: Supported for the limited linkage and tall/wide right-hand sides. The displayed syzygy and equation (10) remain truncated, so this does not supply the requested complete excerpt.
- claim-2: Supported. Theorem 4.4 applies to every valid tuple; \(N\le \min(j,n-r-i)\) and its complementary case are proof branches, not theorem hypotheses. Theorem 4.5 explicitly invokes Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4.
- claim-3: Accurate diagnosis of the supplied ar5iv corruption, but it does not retrieve equations (8)–(10) or Definition 2.1’s complete inequalities.
- claim-4: Correct only as an inventory statement about the supplied search record. The 2024 full-text candidates are identical ar5iv content with the same digest; Crossref supplies metadata, and the other full-text source is the unrelated 2011 paper. No alternate-provider 2024 excerpt was obtained.
- claim-5: Correct. The requested target is **not established**. In particular, the strategy neither obtains the required uncorrupted excerpt nor fully distinguishes valid-tuple hypotheses from reductions used only inside the proof.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Retrieve source-29 from a provider other than ar5iv—such as the native arXiv PDF/source or publisher PDF/HTML—and provide one bounded, digested excerpt containing verbatim: equations (8), (9), and (10); every inequality in Definition 2.1; Lemma 2.5; and Theorems 4.4–4.5. Include stable locators and identify separately (i) valid-tuple conditions inherited as theorem hypotheses and (ii) proof-only branches such as \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) versus \(N>\min(j,n-r-i)\).

## Required revisions
- Do not present the legible linkage as satisfying the full extraction task.
- Record that the alternate-provider requirement was attempted but not fulfilled.
- Explicitly state that “valid \(\varphi\)” is a theorem hypothesis whose complete content remains unavailable, whereas the \(N\)-inequalities in the proof of Theorem 4.4 are not additional theorem restrictions.
